analysis_notes.summary: LM2 Torah 112 is a single-sentence aphorism with no bechina language whatsoever. The full text records that the Rebbe, regarding the subject of strengthening oneself so that a person should not fall in his mind because of the multitude of flaws and corruptions he caused through his actions, answered and said: 'If you believe that they can corrupt, believe that they can repair.' The teaching contains no bechina equalities of the form 'X is an aspect of Y'. The only structural device present is a symmetrical logical implication used as moral encouragement: the capacity to corrupt entails by the same faith the capacity to repair. This is a practical-ethical declaration (eitza-type reasoning by analogy), not an ontological equation between concepts. No concepts are flagged as missing from the dataset because the text does not employ bechina language that would generate dataset nodes.
